Splitting the nodes by the sign of their entries in the leading eigenvector of the modularity matrix gives A, B, C, D (teal) and E, F, G, H (violet), cutting only the two accent edges. The card lists both sides as id sets and the split's modularity, 0.333." width="100%"} Newman's (2006) spectral method: the eigenvector of the largest eigenvalue of the modularity matrix $B = A - k k^T / 2m$ points toward the split with the highest modularity, so nodes are divided by the sign of their entry. It is fast, deterministic and a common first cut for community detection, and the basis of Newman's recursive leading-eigenvector method; apply it again to each side for more communities. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights in the modularity matrix. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[set[int], set[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The two communities as sets of node IDs: nodes with negative entries first, then the rest. The eigenvector's sign is chosen so that the lowest-ID node with a nonzero entry is in the first set. An edgeless graph gives an empty first set. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The modularity matrix is formed densely and fully diagonalized, $O(V^3)$ time. Nodes whose entry is zero (up to $10^{-12}$) go to the second set, as in NetworkX's `spectral_modularity_bipartition`, which returns the same two sets but in an order that depends on the eigensolver's arbitrary sign; NetworkX also ignores edge weights, so use `weighted=False` to match it on weighted graphs. Parallel edges add up. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Zachary's karate club splits almost exactly along the club's real fission: ::: {#7044fd55 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.karate_club() left, right = g.spectral_modularity_bipartition() len(left), len(right), g.modularity([left, right]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (16, 18, 0.37146614069691) ``` ::: :::
